note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA to 12.0 ng/mL despite prior negative biopsy and new PI-RADS 4 lesion on MRI.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer risk assessment. The patient is a 70-year-old retired postal worker, married, living with an adult child in a multi-generational household. He is a current smoker with a 35 pack-year history and cycles five times weekly for commuting. Medical history includes COPD managed with tiotropium and osteoarthritis. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 3/35. Recent appointments include a pain clinic visit for chronic shoulder pain. He prefers morning appointments due to reliance on public transport. PSA has risen significantly from 3.5 ng/mL in October 2024 to 12.0 ng/mL in February 2025, prompting this re-evaluation.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetric, and non-tender with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs. Respiratory auscultation shows mild expiratory wheezing consistent with known COPD.
